description:

Job Title: AI Product Engineer
Requisition ID: R10248050
Location: Cheltenham, UK
Clearance Type: Eligible for SC

What’s your possible?

At Northrop Grumman UK, you are part of a team driving innovation where it matters most, solving tomorrow’s challenges and shaping the technology solutions of the future. It’s what we call Defining Possible.

This mindset goes beyond our customer solutions. It is the foundation for your career development and the impact we have within the community.

This is more than just a job. It’s a mission.

Join our Cyber & Intelligence business and become part of a growing Operational Effects team that is building the next generation of AI-enabled products for national security and government customers.

As an AI Product Engineer, you will help create proprietary software capabilities that deliver operational advantage, strengthen existing programmes, and unlock future growth opportunities. This is a unique opportunity to join at an early stage and play a key role in establishing and scaling a new AI product engineering capability within Northrop Grumman UK.

Working alongside engineers, technical specialists and users, you will take products from concept through to adoption. You will help shape technical direction, influence product strategy, and deliver innovative solutions using modern AI technologies including large language models (LLMs), retrieval augmented generation (RAG), and agentic workflows.

If you enjoy solving real-world problems, experimenting with emerging technologies and building software that has meaningful impact, this could be the opportunity for you.

What you’ll be doing

You will:

- Design, build and maintain AI-enabled software products that support operational mission outcomes.
- Develop capabilities using LLMs, RAG architectures, agentic workflows and other emerging AI technologies.
- Work directly with users and stakeholders to understand challenges and translate requirements into valuable product features.
- Contribute to product roadmaps, software architecture decisions and engineering standards.
- Implement robust engineering practices including testing, CI/CD pipelines, observability and supportability.
- Support technical demonstrations, stakeholder engagement activities, innovation initiatives and recruitment efforts.

What we’re looking for

We are interested in hearing from people who can demonstrate:

- Experience designing, developing or supporting software products or applications.
- Knowledge of modern software engineering practices, including testing, version control and continuous integration.
- Experience or strong interest in AI technologies, machine learning, LLMs, RAG solutions or intelligent automation.
- Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to work through complex technical challenges.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
- The ability to work effectively both independently and within collaborative multidisciplinary teams.

Desirable experience

- Defence, national security, government or advanced technology sector experience.
- Experience developing AI-enabled products or data-driven applications.
- Exposure to cloud-native technologies, modern software architectures and DevOps practices.
- Experience mentoring colleagues or contributing to technical leadership activities.
- Degree qualification in a relevant discipline, although equivalent experience is equally valued.

Even if you do not meet every requirement, we would still encourage you to apply. We value diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives, and recognise that great potential can come from many different career paths.

Security Clearance

Due to the nature of our work, you must be a British Citizen to be considered for this opportunity.

You must be able to gain and maintain UK Government Security Check (SC) clearance.

Our recruitment team is on hand to answer any questions and will guide you through the process: talentenquiries@uk.ngc.com

Benefits

At Northrop Grumman UK, we offer a competitive rewards package designed to support your wellbeing, career development and lifestyle, including:

- Flexible working options, including compressed fortnight arrangements where applicable
- Private healthcare
- Cash health plan
- Annual performance bonus opportunities
- Holiday buy and sell scheme
- Career development and learning programmes
- Professional accreditation support
- Pension scheme
- Employee assistance programme
- Inclusive employee networks and communities

Why Join Us?

A Mission to Believe In

Every day, our teams contribute to building a more secure and connected world. Whether developing innovative AI solutions or solving complex operational challenges, your work will have meaningful real-world impact.

A Place to Belong and Thrive

We believe innovation is driven by diverse perspectives and experiences. Every voice matters at our table, and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can contribute, grow and succeed.

Your Career, Your Way

As our AI product engineering capability expands, so too will the opportunities available to you. Whether you want to deepen your technical expertise, develop as a leader, or explore emerging technologies, you'll have the support and development needed to shape your own career journey.

Ready to Apply?

Yes – Submit your application online today.

Possibly – Want to learn more? Contact our team at talentenquiries@uk.ngc.com

No – Explore our other opportunities across Northrop Grumman UK. We are growing across the UK and are always looking for talented people who want to help us define possible.

Northrop Grumman is committed to hiring and retaining a diverse workforce, and encourages individuals from all backgrounds and all abilities to apply and consider becoming a part of our diverse and inclusive workforce.

Northrop Grumman Mission Systems is seeking Logistics Inventory and Control Coordinator B to join its team of qualified, diverse individuals to support its organization. This position is located in Baltimore, MD.

Primary Function

Compiles records concerned with quantity, cost, and type of material received, in stock, or issued. Requisition needed supplies; verifies material received to determine irregularities in order. Process administrative receipts. Pulls materials from bins, adhering to special handling requirements. Consolidates and verifies all outbound material for accuracy and adherence to guidelines. Performs bin checks as required to validate inventory counts. Assists in shelf-life process and coordinates with lab personnel to ensure adherence to requirements. Maintaining good communication across various departments and vendors. Identify areas of process improvement with a focus on digital transformation.

Tools and Equipment
Operate forklifts, pallet jacks, scissor lifts. Precision parts counting scale, x-ray parts counter, and other electronic manufacturing equipment as needed. Temperature control equipment for temperature-sensitive material. Storage and retrieval systems (such as VLM, Autostores). Tools such as, measuring tapes, , heat and vacuum sealers, etc. CADSTAR, MPLM software.

Materials
Sensitive electronic components, hazardous materials, temperature-sensitive electronic components (including sub-freezing handling), shelf-life, secured material, classified material, moisture-sensitive material, batch-managed material. Bulk material intake and movement.

Working procedure and/or responsibility assigned:

1. Dock management – loading and unloading of material, including proper maintenance and handling of sensitive electronic components, hazardous material, secured and classified material, and other specialized material handling as required. Separating product into internal and external locations; sort and stage by scanning materials appropriately.

2. Receiving - Verify packing slip to validate purchase order and line item, material received and quantity, packaging, and delivery condition; process receipt transactions as required. Sort and stage material as appropriate. Maintain storage conditions of deliveries, such as temperature control, hazardous materials, etc. Perform de-trashing or repackaging of material as needed.

3. Put-Away / Re-induction – Bin materials based on special handling requirements, size and dimension, and current inventory. Perform necessary systematic transactions to maintain inventory physical location accuracy.

4. Picking – Pull material from designated locations as directed by paperwork (may include hand-counting, measuring, scale-count, x-ray, etc.). Repackage and transfer material maintaining special handling requirements. Enter system transactions throughout the process to maintain accurate material tracking. Perform de-trashing or repackaging of material as needed. Sort and stage material as appropriate. Managing material adhering to special-handling requirements.

5. Consolidating – Audit pulled material by checking part marking, part number, batch validation (if applicable), quantity (count or measure), and packaging (special handling requirements). Cross-reference quantity pulled versus systematic transaction. Use CADSTAR, MLPM, or other material management system as required. Troubleshoot and resolve issues identified during audit. Ensure all material is present and accounted for prior to processing to next step. Perform systematic transactions for outbound delivery. Sort and stage material as appropriate. Manage material adhering to special-handling requirements. Prepare paperwork for factory use as determined by specialized processes.

6. Inventory Management – Perform DCMA cycle-counts, adhering to compliance on DFARS, ISO, AS9100, batch management. Troubleshoot and resolve inventory discrepancies. Exercise sound judgement in finding and resolving critical issues; Have confidence/trust to make the right decision – attempt to solve before escalating but know when to escalate. Manage specific bin locations to maintain and restore material requirements using tools including, but not limited to those described above (such as ovens). Assist in projects to optimize inventory for external customer requirements.

7. Order Management – Convert planned orders, create kits, request labels, and maintain production orders to latest revision as directed. Release production orders to manufacturing in support of factory readiness.

8. Provide assistance to other coordinators as assigned.

This is an SEA Union represented position.

This is a 2nd Shift position.

Education requirement(s):

- Associate degree; or,

- In lieu of an associate’s degree, sixty (60) credit hours, including at least nine (9) credit hours in Math, Science, and/or IT courses, and three years’ experience in Inventory Management, Production Control, and/or Receiving in a warehouse / manufacturing environment; or,

- In lieu of associates degree or credit hours, six (6) years’ experience in Inventory Management, Production Control, and/or Receiving in a warehouse / manufacturing environment.

Experience requirement(s)

- Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite Applications, with an emphasis on Excel. MRP/ERP business experience (SAP preferred) and

- Three years’ of experience in Inventory Management, Production Control, and/or Receiving in a warehouse / manufacturing environment.

Other Requirements:

- Must acquire globally recognized ASCM Warehouse Certificate or ASCM Certification (either Certified in Planning and Inventory Management (CPIM) or Certified Supply Chain Certification (CSCP)) within twelve (12) months of employment. Failure to do so will result in release from employment.
